thread:
Alex W: quick follow-up to the tiering idea I sketched yesterday — thinking about a hot/cold prefix segmentation that lives inside the same slab allocator rather than separate slab pools. goal: cheaper demotion paths and fewer cross-node moves. thoughts?

Tess: interesting. do you mean mark prefixes as "hot" at access-time and move them into a compacted hot region in the slab? or just change eviction priority?

Alex W: avoid full move if possible. proposal is soft-tiering: keep same physical slab but maintain a hot index (bitmap + small LRU) that changes eviction weight. demote by lowering priority and letting normal eviction pick them off.

Miguel: soft-tiering sounds cheaper for handoffs, but how do we preserve read-after-write correctness? if hot prefix falls back mid-write we could see stale versions in short window.

Alex W: good call. plan is to couple tier changes with a cheap fence token cached in the prefix header. invariant: any write bumps a generation; any demote must publish the new gen. readers verify gen before trusting cached KV. if mismatch, fallback to RPC.

Samir: hmm generation checks add a roundtrip in some paths. is that on hot read-critical path?

Alex W: we only check gen when we hit the index-bit transition or when we observe a tombstone/fence marker. common hot reads skip the check. it's rare.

Tess: how do we score hotness? open to counters, recency, or decay model. counters blow up space.

Miguel: what about using the existing access sampler we have for prefix telemetry? sample hits to decide promotion, and use exponential decay to avoid counters. cheap and already in telemetry pipeline.

Samir: promotion policy ok, but eviction fairness is tricky in multi-tenant. if hotset bias is too strong small tenants can hog hot bucket. need per-tenant dampening.

Alex W: agreed — plan: per-tenant hot credit. tenant gets credits proportional to SLA/weight; promotions consume credits; background reclaim returns credits as access decays. prevents single tenant hog.

InfraBot: deploy note: rollout must be feature-flagged and gated by evict-metrics: hot-residency / hot-steal-rate / generation-mismatch-rate. default off.

Tess: ops question — observability. add metrics: hot_promote_count, hot_demote_count, demote_write_conflicts, gen_mismatch_rate. traces for promotion path.

Miguel: runtime complexity: adding bitmap + small LRU per slab increases metadata by ~3-4 bytes / prefix. acceptable? our math says yes for our 64B header. need bench.

Samir: QA: simulate churned tenants to ensure demote tail latency doesn't spike. also test canary that forces rapid toggling to detect oscillation.

Alex W: agreed on tests. next steps: I'll draft short RFC with API: prefix.header.gen, prefix.header.hotbit, promotion RPC (idempotent), and per-tenant credit lease. want a quick sync Wed 11?

Tess: I'm in. can you dump a prototype mem-layout so infra can eyeball?

Alex W: will post layout + microbench by Tue EOD. thanks all :+1:

Miguel: one more: consider an escape hatch where if gen_mismatch_rate > threshold we fall back to strict handoff mode (full ownership transfer). saves correctness during weird races.

Samir: +1 to escape hatch. avoid global outages.

Alex W: noted — include escape hatch and rollout gates in the RFC. thanks everyone.

InfraBot: reminder: create RFC doc in repo at /rfc/ before Wed sync.
